interpretations.scope_one_line: Build a net-new HTTP REST API service for managing orders: CRUD over an Order resource backed by a datastore, with validation and persistence.
in_scope: A REST service exposing order endpoints: POST /orders (create), GET /orders (list, paginated/filterable), GET /orders/{id} (fetch one), PATCH/PUT /orders/{id} (update), DELETE or status-transition to cancel
An Order domain model: id, customer reference, line items (product/sku, quantity, unit price), status (e.g. pending/paid/shipped/cancelled), totals, timestamps
Request/response DTOs with input validation (required fields, positive quantities, non-empty line items) returning structured 4xx errors
A persistence layer (repository/data-access) over a relational DB with a schema/migration for orders and order line items
Status lifecycle transitions enforced server-side (e.g. cannot ship a cancelled order)
Wiring: controller/handler layer -> service/business layer -> repository, plus app bootstrap/config and a health endpoint
Automated tests: unit tests for the service/validation and integration tests hitting the API endpoints
API documentation (OpenAPI/Swagger or equivalent) describing the endpoints
comparison_surfaces: HTTP controller / route handler layer (request parsing, status codes, error mapping)
Service / business-logic layer (validation, order-total computation, status-transition rules)
Data-access / repository layer + DB schema and migrations
Application bootstrap / config (DB connection, server startup, env config)
key_behaviors: Creating an order validates the payload (non-empty line items, positive quantities, known customer) and rejects invalid input with a 4xx and a structured error body
Order total is computed server-side from line items, never trusted from the client
Each order gets a server-assigned unique id and created/updated timestamps
Listing orders supports filtering (e.g. by status/customer) and pagination
Fetching or mutating a non-existent order id returns 404
Status transitions are validated against an allowed state machine; illegal transitions are rejected
Persistence is durable and atomic — an order and its line items are written/rolled back together (transactional)
Endpoints return correct HTTP semantics (201 on create with Location/id, 200 on read, 204/200 on update, 404/409 on conflict)
assumptions_i_had_to_make: This is net-new development (scaffold-api), NOT a migration of an existing service — the request says 'build', names no legacy source, and gives no service to port

Tech stack is unspecified; I assume the repo's configured target/generation-spec stack (the dotnet-service spec referenced in examples/, i.e. a .NET service), defaulting to a conventional layered web API if no config is found
'Orders' means a commerce order resource (customer + line items + status), not 'ordering/sorting' or some domain-specific meaning
Backing store is a relational database (the conventional default); no specific DB engine was named
Synchronous REST/JSON over HTTP is intended — not gRPC, GraphQL, or an event-driven/async-messaging API
AuthN/AuthZ, payment processing, inventory reservation, and notifications are out of scope unless added later — the request scopes only the orders API itself
Single-service scope: no separate customer/product service is built; those are referenced by id only
It is a brand-new project skeleton (no existing codebase to extend, since this repo is the framework source, not a service repo)

interpretations.scope_one_line: Build a net-new RESTful HTTP service exposing CRUD-plus-lifecycle endpoints for customer orders, backed by a persistence layer, with create/read/list/update-status/cancel as the core operations.
in_scope: A REST resource at /orders with POST (create), GET /orders/{id} (read one), GET /orders (list with pagination/filtering), and a status-transition/cancel operation
An Order domain model: id, customer reference, line items (product, quantity, unit price), totals, status (e.g. PENDING/PAID/SHIPPED/CANCELLED), timestamps
Request validation and structured error responses (400 on bad input, 404 on missing order, 409 on illegal status transition)
A persistence layer (repository/DAO over a relational DB) with schema/migration for orders and order line items
JSON request/response serialization and a documented wire contract
Order status state machine enforcing legal transitions (create -> pay -> ship; cancel only before shipped)
Automated tests: unit tests for domain/validation/state-machine and integration tests for the endpoints
Basic operational surface: health endpoint, config, and run/build instructions
comparison_surfaces: HTTP controller / route layer (request parsing, status codes, response shaping)
Service / domain layer (order creation, total calculation, status state machine, business rules)
Data-access layer (repository over relational DB, schema + migrations)
Wire-format / API contract (JSON DTOs, error envelope, pagination shape)
Auth boundary (assumed token/identity check on write endpoints, stubbed if unspecified)
key_behaviors: Creating an order validates the payload, computes totals from line items, persists it, and returns 201 with the created resource and its id
Status transitions are enforced by a state machine; an illegal transition (e.g. cancel an already-shipped order) returns 409 rather than mutating state
Reads return 404 for unknown ids; list supports pagination and at minimum status/customer filtering
Writes are atomic at the persistence layer (order + its line items committed together)
All inputs are validated server-side; malformed/invalid requests fail with 400 and a structured error body, never a 500
Money/quantity arithmetic is exact and consistent between request, stored record, and response
assumptions_i_had_to_make: This is net-new development (scaffold-api territory), not a migration of an existing service
Synchronous REST/JSON over HTTP is intended (not gRPC, GraphQL, or an event/async API)
A single-service, single relational database design is acceptable; no microservice decomposition, payment-gateway integration, or inventory service is required unless asked
The stack/framework follows the repo's configured target generation spec (e.g. .NET/Spring-style service) rather than a language the user names, since none was given
'Orders' means customer purchase orders with line items, not work orders or another domain
Persistence is durable (a real DB with migrations), not in-memory, even for a first cut

interpretations.scope_one_line: Build a net-new HTTP REST API for managing orders — CRUD endpoints over an orders resource backed by persistence — scaffolded from scratch as a new service.
in_scope: A REST resource at /orders with the standard verbs: POST /orders (create), GET /orders (list, paginated), GET /orders/{id} (fetch one), PATCH/PUT /orders/{id} (update/status change), DELETE or cancel /orders/{id}
An Order domain model: id, line items (product/sku, quantity, price), customer reference, status (e.g. pending/paid/shipped/cancelled), total amount, created/updated timestamps
A persistence layer for orders (repository/DAO over a database) with schema/migration for the orders + order_items tables
Request/response DTOs with input validation (non-empty items, positive quantities/prices) and structured error responses (400/404/409/422)
Service/business layer computing order totals and enforcing legal status transitions
Wiring/bootstrap: routing, dependency injection, app entrypoint so the service runs and serves the endpoints
Tests for the endpoints and the order lifecycle (create -> read -> update status)
comparison_surfaces: DTO / wire-format layer (request + response schemas, validation, error envelope)
Service / domain layer (Order model, total calculation, status-transition rules)
Application bootstrap / DI / config (entrypoint, server wiring)
key_behaviors: Create an order with one or more line items and return 201 with the created order including a generated id and computed total
Reject invalid create payloads (empty items, non-positive quantity/price, missing customer) with a 4xx validation error rather than persisting
List orders and fetch a single order by id, returning 404 for unknown ids
Update an order's status only along legal transitions (e.g. cannot ship a cancelled order) — reject illegal transitions with 409/422
Order total is derived server-side from line items, never trusted from the client
Each order is persisted durably and survives across requests (real repository, not in-memory mock as the shipped path)

interpretations.scope_one_line: Build a net-new RESTful HTTP service that manages customer orders — create, read, list, update, and cancel orders — backed by persistent storage.
in_scope: CRUD-plus endpoints for an Order resource: POST /orders (create), GET /orders/{id} (fetch one), GET /orders (list with pagination/filtering), PATCH /orders/{id} (update status/fields), DELETE or POST /orders/{id}/cancel (cancel)
Order domain model: id, customer reference, line items (product id, quantity, unit price), status enum (pending/paid/shipped/cancelled), totals, timestamps
Order line-item handling and order-total computation
Request validation and structured error responses (400 on bad input, 404 on missing order, 409 on illegal status transition)
Persistence layer / data access for orders and line items (repository over a relational DB)
Order status lifecycle / state-transition rules
JSON wire format for requests and responses
Basic automated tests covering the endpoints and the status-transition rules
comparison_surfaces: service / domain layer (order lifecycle + total calculation)
data-access layer (order + line-item repository over a DB)
key_behaviors: Creating an order persists it with a server-assigned id and an initial status of 'pending'
Order total is derived from line items (sum of quantity x unit price), not trusted from the client
Status transitions are validated — only legal transitions allowed; an illegal transition (e.g. cancel an already-shipped order) returns 409
GET on a non-existent order id returns 404, not a 500 or empty 200
List endpoint supports pagination and is bounded (no unbounded full-table dump)
Invalid create/update payloads are rejected with 400 and a descriptive error body before touching the DB
Each order is uniquely addressable and reads reflect the last committed write
assumptions_i_had_to_make: 'API' means a synchronous RESTful HTTP/JSON service (not GraphQL, gRPC, or an internal library)
The resource is customer purchase orders (e-commerce sense), not work orders or some other order domain
Standard CRUD lifecycle is wanted even though only 'orders' was named — create/read/list plus status updates and cancel
Persistence is expected (a real datastore), not an in-memory stub
Stack/framework is unspecified — I would follow this repo's scaffold-api target patterns / generation spec (the dotnet-service spec) unless told otherwise
Auth, payment processing, inventory reservation, and async event publishing are out of scope unless requested — this is the order-record CRUD surface only
Single-tenant, single-service scope; no multi-service orchestration or saga
Backward compatibility is not a concern since this is net-new
